definition: A place or scene of wild uproar and chaos; originally, the capital of Hell in Milton's epic.
origin: Coined by John Milton in Paradise Lost (1667), from Greek pan (all) + daimōn (demon, spirit).

source.author: John Milton
source.quote: Anon out of the earth a Fabrick huge / Rose like an Exhalation, with the sound / Of Dulcet Symphonies and voices sweet, / Built like a Temple, where Pilasters round / Were set, and Doric pillars overlaid / With Golden Architrave; nor did there want / Cornice or Freeze, with sculptured Ornaments, / And all this in dark outside; nor less / Within. Above them all the Arch-Angel stood, / And from another side th' officious Roosts / Of Pandas, and the Sons of God, and Thrones / In order stood; and from the other side / Satan with his vast host; when lo! between / Two such amazing Armies, a third rose / As a third Host, and in the midst a place / Of Palaces and Towrs, and call'd it / Pandæmonium, the high Capital / Of Satan and his Peers.

definition: The code of knightly honour, courage, courtesy, and martial skill; the ideals of the medieval knight.
origin: From Old French chevalerie (knighthood, horsemanship); in The Knight's Tale (c. 1390) Theseus wins kingdoms through wisdom and chivalrye, and the Knight embodies the ideal throughout the tale.
